title: Trump Endorses Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for Reelection
carouselSummary:
Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 election.
The move comes amid deepening regional tensions.
summary: US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's reelection campaign ahead of Israel's October 27 national election.
author: Mashkoora Khan and Nischai Vats

detailContent.heading: Trump endorses Netanyahu
paragraphs: Donald Trump publicly backed Benjamin Netanyahu's reelection campaign ahead of Israel's October 27 vote. The endorsement is notable as the first national election since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.

Trump described Netanyahu as a strong partner in opposing Iran. The report notes Trump's earlier support for Netanyahu and his request to Israel's president to consider a pardon in the corruption cases against him.

detailContent.heading: Regional issues remain in focus
paragraphs: The report also described tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, including competing claims by Iran and the United States about whether the shipping route was open and reports of attacks on commercial vessels.
Separately, Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia were advised to follow local emergency warnings and move to a safe indoor location when alerts are issued.

detailContent.heading: Domestic political pressure
paragraphs: The endorsement comes as Netanyahu faces a closely watched campaign and continuing political controversy at home. The report also described wider regional security concerns.

title: Xi Jinping Says China Is Willing to Work With Trump on China-US Ties
carouselSummary:
Xi says China and the US should work together as partners.
The leaders are discussing trade, security and technology.
imageAlt: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping at the White House
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for China and the United States to be partners rather than rivals during his state visit to Washington.
author: Merin Varghese and Nischai Vats

detailContent.heading: Xi calls for cooperation
paragraphs: During a three-day state visit to the United States, Xi Jinping said China and the US should seek to be partners rather than rivals. He called for a stable relationship that allows cooperation while managing competition and differences.
Xi said the interests of the two countries are connected and that their national goals could complement one another.

detailContent.heading: Issues on the agenda
paragraphs: The leaders were expected to discuss trade, Iran, Taiwan and artificial intelligence. The report noted that a trade truce had been extended, while differences remained over tariffs, rare-earth exports and advanced technology.

detailContent.heading: Other regional developments
paragraphs: The report also covered Pakistan's claim that it had carried out strikes on sites in Afghanistan, and the Taliban's denial that Afghan forces had attacked Pakistan.

title: Mhasrul Police Arrest Cybercriminal Linked to 38 Cases
shortTitle: Nashik Police Arrest Cyber Fraud Suspect
carouselSummary:
A suspect accused of a job-fraud operation was arrested.
Investigators link the case to 38 cybercrime complaints.
imageAlt: Image accompanying a report on the Mhasrul cybercrime arrest
summary: Police in Nashik arrested a suspect accused of running a job-fraud operation and linked by investigators to 38 cybercrime cases.
author: Santosh Sonawane

detailContent.heading: Suspect arrested in job-fraud investigation
paragraphs: Mhasrul Police in Nashik arrested a 24-year-old suspect accused of operating a job-fraud network across India. Investigators said digital-trail checks linked the suspect to 38 cybercrime complaints registered in different districts.
The case began after a complainant reported losing ₹6.45 lakh to a fake recruiter who offered employment through an app.

detailContent.heading: How investigators tracked the case
paragraphs: Police examined phone numbers and email accounts connected with the alleged fraud, then used location information to find the suspect. Officers seized mobile phones, SIM cards, bank cards and chequebooks during the operation.
The suspect was produced in court and remanded to police custody while the investigation continued.

title: How Delhi's AI Traffic Signals on 42 Corridors May Improve Traffic Flow
carouselSummary:
AI traffic management is planned for 42 Delhi corridors.
Simulations suggest some routes could see shorter delays.
imageAlt: Traffic congestion on a Delhi road
summary: A Delhi Traffic Police simulation suggests that an AI-backed traffic management system could reduce delays on some corridors, while the busiest roads may see more modest gains.
author: Hemani Bhandari

detailContent.heading: AI traffic management planned for 42 corridors
paragraphs: Delhi's Integrated Traffic Management System is planned for an initial group of 42 road corridors. The list includes Nelson Mandela Road, Press Enclave Road, Africa Avenue, Mahipalpur and sections of Mehrauli-Gurgaon Road.
Ring Road, Outer Ring Road and the DND Flyway–Ghazipur Road corridor are also included in the first phase.

detailContent.heading: Simulation estimates vary by route
paragraphs: A Delhi Traffic Police simulation projects that some stretches could see delays fall by around 40%, with travel times reduced by more than 25%. The estimated gains differ across the network.
The report cautions that heavily congested arterial routes may see more modest improvements than some other corridors.

title: France's Government Under Pressure After Weekend of Widespread Violence
shortTitle: France Faces Pressure After Weekend Violence
carouselSummary:
Macron calls for calm after protests turned violent.
Officials face questions over public safety and unrest.
imageAlt: French President Emmanuel Macron speaking after weekend violence
summary: France's government is under pressure after widespread looting and violence followed protests over living costs and public services.
author: Katya Adler

detailContent.heading: Government responds to weekend unrest
paragraphs: France's prime minister called a crisis cabinet meeting after protests over living costs and public services were followed by looting and clashes. President Emmanuel Macron urged calm in a televised address.
France's interior minister offered to resign, but Macron instead asked him to review public safety and pursue those responsible for the violence.

detailContent.heading: Scale of damage and criticism
paragraphs: The report said around 1,500 shops and businesses were looted or damaged and about 1,000 police officers were injured, including seven seriously. Political opponents and unions questioned whether authorities were adequately prepared.
The unrest has intensified questions about public services, compensation for businesses and how future demonstrations will be managed.

detailContent.heading: Political pressure continues
paragraphs: France's parliament remains divided, while concerns about public debt complicate decisions on spending and welfare. A contested presidential race is also adding to the political pressure.

title: Microsoft Pulls Out of UK's Largest AI Data Centre
shortTitle: Microsoft Exits UK AI Data Centre Project
carouselSummary:
Microsoft has ended its involvement in the Loughton project.
Developer Nscale says it remains committed to building it.
imageAlt: Illustration of the planned AI data centre in Loughton, Essex
summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from funding a planned AI data centre in Essex, while developer Nscale says it remains committed to the project.
author: Alice Cunningham

detailContent.heading: Microsoft exits the Loughton project
paragraphs: Microsoft has ended its involvement in a planned £2bn AI data centre in Loughton, Essex. The company had been expected to fund a supercomputer at the site.
Nscale said it remains committed to the project and is exploring alternative power sources. It also said its wider relationship with Microsoft continues on projects in other countries.

detailContent.heading: Power connection delay
paragraphs: The data centre had been expected to receive power by the end of the year, but the BBC reported that the connection may not be available until the 2030s.
The planned facility is expected to create about 250 permanent jobs when it opens.

detailContent.heading: Wider UK investment
paragraphs: The report noted Microsoft's recent announcement of a wider UK investment package, part of which had been intended to support the Loughton supercomputer.

title: The Genetic Technique That Finds Almost Every Infection
carouselSummary:
Metagenomic tests can identify known and unknown pathogens.
AI may help doctors get results faster and guide care.
summary: Metagenomic testing can detect a wide range of pathogens in patient samples, helping doctors diagnose difficult infections and guide treatment.
author: David Cox

detailContent.heading: Testing looks beyond known pathogens
paragraphs: Metagenomic testing analyses genetic material in a sample without limiting the search to microbes doctors already expect to find. The approach helped researchers identify the virus behind the first known COVID-19 cases.
In hospitals, it may help investigate severe or unexplained illnesses when routine tests do not provide an answer.

detailContent.heading: Potential to guide urgent treatment
paragraphs: The article describes cases where testing of cerebrospinal fluid helped distinguish an infection from other possible causes of symptoms, including one patient whose diagnosis avoided an unnecessary transplant.
Faster sequencing and AI-assisted analysis may help clinicians interpret complex results sooner, although separating meaningful signals from contamination and harmless microbes remains important.

detailContent.heading: Possible public-health applications
paragraphs: Pilot hospital work found that metagenomic tests could identify some pathogens not detected by routine testing. The method is also being explored for monitoring sewage and air samples for emerging infections.

title: Was Neanderthal Life Violent? This Wound Suggests Lethal Fighting Was More Common
shortTitle: Neanderthal Wound Offers Clue to Ancient Violence
carouselSummary:
A 75,000-year-old shoulder blade bears a round wound.
Researchers say a wooden spear may have caused it.
imageAlt: A Neanderthal shoulder blade with a small round hole
summary: A wound in a Neanderthal shoulder blade may be evidence of a wooden spear strike 75,000 years ago, although researchers say a hunting accident is also possible.
author: Pallab Ghosh

detailContent.heading: A wound in a 75,000-year-old skeleton
paragraphs: Researchers examining Neanderthal remains from Shanidar Cave in Iraqi Kurdistan found a near-circular hole in a shoulder blade. They say its shape and position are consistent with an injury caused by a sharpened wooden spear.
The wound may be among the earliest evidence of a potentially lethal spear injury in the region.

detailContent.heading: Accident or interpersonal violence?
paragraphs: Researchers have not ruled out an accident during a hunt. Other experts cited in the report consider an attack plausible based on the wound's position and extent.
The evidence adds to discoveries of injuries among ancient human relatives, but cannot by itself establish how common violence was in Neanderthal communities.

detailContent.heading: A wider debate about ancient violence
paragraphs: Findings from other archaeological sites suggest that deadly violence occurred long before farming and permanent settlements. Researchers continue to debate how often individual attacks occurred and when they became organized conflict.
